intro: Sometimes you don't need to change mountains. It's enough to pause on the trail and ask yourself the right questions.
cierre: This is what you answered at this rest stop on the trail. Read it again next month: you'll see how far you've climbed.

VOL: What small step have you been dodging for days, and what would happen if you took it tomorrow before breakfast?
If your body could write you a letter, what would it thank you for and what would it ask of you?
At what time of day does your strength slip away, and what would protect it?
What promise did you make yourself and quietly let fall? Is it worth picking back up?
When no one is watching, who are you on the climb?
What habit are you carrying in your backpack that weighs more than it gives?
MAE: What would you love to master so well that you could teach it without notes?
What did you learn this month that the you of a year ago didn't know?
If you had a mountain guide for your craft today, what would you ask them first?
Where are you afraid of becoming a beginner again?
What recent mistake taught you more than a success?
What would you give one hour a day to if you knew that in five years you'd be among the best?
VOZ: What truth of yours do you still not dare to say out loud?
If your message fit in a single sentence carved into a stone at the summit, what would it be?
Who did you stay silent with when you wanted to speak?
What story from your life could encourage someone who is just starting to climb?
Where do you sound like yourself, and where do you sound like what others expect of you?
What unfinished conversation would make your backpack lighter?
VAL: If your money could talk, would it say it works for your summit or for your anxiety?
What recent purchase pulled you away from your peak, and which one brought you closer?
What is an hour of your life worth, and what are you trading it for?
What value do you give others that you still don't dare to charge for?
If you had six months of savings tomorrow, what decision would you make that you're not making today?
What were you taught about money that you no longer want to keep believing?
EVO: What part of the you from five years ago would be surprised to see you today?
What version of yourself are you leaving behind on this stretch of the trail?
What belief about yourself no longer fits you?
If this year were a chapter in your book, what title would you give it?
What fall made you stronger than you admit?
What would the child you once were say, seeing how you live today?
TRA: What do you want to remain when you are no longer on the mountain?
Who are you clearing a path for, even if they don't know it yet?
If your life were a trail others will walk, what marker would you leave on the hardest stretch?
What cause would get you up early without anyone asking?
What would you do differently this year if you knew someone was watching you to learn?
What will people thank you for twenty years from now?
CON: What activity in your life moves your body, your mind and your purpose all at once?
Where do what you love, what you're good at and what the world needs meet?
Which two of your goals compete with each other, and how could they walk together?
If you had to choose a single project that unites your six paths, what would it be?
What moment this week made you feel whole, with no loose pieces?
What are you doing separately that you could do all at once?
CAM: Who holds the rope when you slip?
Who do you owe a call just to say thank you?
Who would you like to rope up with this year?
Which relationship takes more oxygen from you than it gives?
How is your base camp: your home, your rest, your people?
Who could you walk alongside on their climb this week?
CUMBRE: If you reached your summit today, who would be with you in the photo?
Is your summit still yours, or is it the one others expected of you?
If the you of ten years from now read about your day today, what would they thank you for?
What would you do tomorrow if you knew fear couldn't follow you?
What would you give up to become who you truly want to be?
If you had only one year of trail left, would you keep climbing this same mountain?
